newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM says 8.0 pct growth achievable in '97.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM says 8.0 pct growth achievable in '97.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said late on Thursday that the Gross Domestic Product growth rate of 8.0 percent for 1997 was achievable for the booming economy.
The eight percent rate of growth sustainable for the next 30 years, the national Bernama news agency quoted the prime minister as saying in his parliamentary constituency in northern Kedah state.
"We will achieve it by continuing with the way we manage our economy since 1987," he said.

Malaysia has logged an average GDP growth of eight percent for the last decade. The prime minister has set a target of becoming a fully developed nation by the year 2020, which economists say requires an annual growth of eight percent.
Mahathir said slowing down the economies of the region was one of the aims of speculators who have been selling down currencies of Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines recently.
"They (speculators) said the region's growth should be slowed down because the economies are overheating. They want the inflation rate to be higher and the poor countries to get poorer," he said.
"They interfere in the region's economies because they want to make sure what they say is (proved) true," he added.
Some economists have said Malaysia's economy may be overheating due to sagging exports, a huge current account deficit and a domestic demand-supply gap.
In the last one month currency speculators have pulled down the Malaysian ringgit by over 11 percent against the U.S. dollar on economic fears.
